canonical_statement: Let u on R^n belong to L^q and have all order-m classical partial derivatives in L^r, where n > 0, 0 <= j < m, and 1 <= q,r <= infinity. For j/m <= a <= 1 and 1/p = j/n + a(1/r-m/n) + (1-a)/q, there is a constant depending only on n,m,j,q,r,a such that the maximum L^p norm of the order-j partial derivatives is at most C times the a power of the maximum order-m L^r norm times the (1-a) power of the L^q norm, subject to Nirenberg's two printed endpoint exceptions.

source_selection.work: Louis Nirenberg, On elliptic partial differential equations, Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, series 3, 13(2), 1959, 115-162
source_selection.pinpoint: Lecture II, theorem, page 125, formulae (2.2) and (2.3)

domain_and_universes: n,m,j : Nat; q,r,p : ENNReal; a : Real; u : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real; all declarations in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: if 1 < r < infinity and m-j-n/r is a nonnegative integer, then a < 1
u is C^m, and its order-zero L^q and order-m L^r seminorm maxima are finite
if j=0, r*m<n, and q=infinity, u tends to zero at infinity or belongs to some finite positive L^qTilde
conclusion: The maximum L^p norm of all ordered coordinate derivatives of order j is at most C * |D^m u|_r^a * |u|_q^(1-a).

encoding_decisions.derivatives: Classical iterated Frechet derivatives evaluated on ordered standard-basis directions; the finite supremum realizes the source's maximum over all partial derivatives of a fixed order.
encoding_decisions.regularity: ContDiff Real m supplies the classical derivatives used by the selected source theorem.
encoding_decisions.norms: Mathlib eLpNorm with Lebesgue volume and ENNReal exponents, so q and r can equal infinity.
encoding_decisions.constant_scope: The NNReal constant follows all structural parameters but precedes u, exactly enforcing independence from u.
encoding_decisions.source_exception_1: Decay through the cocompact filter or membership in some finite positive L^qTilde.
encoding_decisions.source_exception_2: The endpoint a=1 is excluded precisely under the source's finite-r nonnegative-integer condition.

degenerate_cases: Dimension zero and j >= m are excluded. The endpoints q=1, r=1, q=infinity, r=infinity, a=j/m, and a=1 otherwise remain admitted. The zero function is admitted. Ordered repeated coordinate directions are retained, and the order-zero derivative is definitionally u.
